metadata.title: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [25. Juni 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.140

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [25. Juni 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.140
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.140
- Datum: 25.6.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
New York, 25.6.41

Dear Hanna,
We have finally found a house for the summer,
which meets all our requirements as „house-workers“ and car-less
people, which is nicely situated and even very near Eva. It
is
7 RAMAPO Road
Ossining, N.Y.
and ten minutes drive from Croton and there is even an
hourly bus-service between Croton and Ossining. I advised
Stefan against cabling the address (which will be valid
from July 1st to Sept. 1st) because you would certainly
think that Ramapo Road is mis-spelt. Actually it is
an old Indian name. One of the great attractions of
the house - besides being nice and near to Eva - was
the fact that the maid will stay on with us and is
even glad to remain, just as glad as I am to be able
to take her over. As we move out in 6 days you can imagine
that we will be busy, packing, arranging things, seeing some
people and trying not to see others and so on. It is 50 minutes
by train from New York and we shall come in now and then
- certainly I because I can thus continue my injections
without changing the doctor. I am glad about this for a
few weeks ago I had some strong reactions against my own
and apparently quite powerful bacterias, and I feel better to
be with a doctor who has experience and is not surprised by
such symptoms which as he says are rather favorable and
even desirable. - I went out Sunday to see Eva and
my sister-in-law came with me to visit her. She found her
looking splendid; she is sunburnt, strong and has grown.
It was only a pity that it was such a rush owing to
the house-hunting, but as we will now be very near to
each other this little disappointment was worth while.
We have not yet heard from you this week although we
had a number of English letters on Sunday. Now it is soon July
and then Manfred will finish his studies and you, I hope are
through with the dentist. We shall then enjoy the idea of knowing
you both in Bath.
Love, kisses Lotte
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Anmerkungen am rechten Rand (x 'not care free') wurden bei der Transkription in den Textfluss integriert bzw. als Randnotiz erkannt.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift ist klar. Die Archiv-Skalen auf Seite 3 verdecken Teile des Textes, dieser ist jedoch durch den Vergleich mit Seite 1 vollständig rekonstruierbar.
